messages:
Maya: FYI bringing up ridgeback18b v1-int6 on canary fleet, seeing intermittent OOMs during multi-turns. Logs attached below.
Jonah: thanks — are these OOMs during warmstart or sustained gen?
Maya: warmstart + spikes when user provides long history (~4k tokens) + default max_new_tokens=512. We hit slab allocation failures on two different host types.
Priya: can you paste the exact error snippet?
Maya: `RuntimeError: cuda out of memory while allocating 536870912 bytes (allocation info: ... slab free 128MB)`
Jonah: hm that looks like fragmentation rather than absolute memory pressure. Ridgeback's layer sizes seem to trigger slab fragmentation with int6 packing.
Alec: any quality hit if we bump to int8 for canary? Product wants minimal regressions for customer-facing demos.
Maya: evals show ~0.6% bleu-ish drop on our internal QA set when going to int8 HYBRID vs int6, but int6 -> int4 had much bigger regressions. int6 seems best perf/quality balance, but frag is bad.
Jonah: concrete mitigations to try: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 256 for canary 2) enable soft-slot-reserve 3) bump slab compaction frequency 4) enable KV-prefix evict threshold for long histories.
Priya: order of operations: we should avoid mass rollback. Suggest route: patch canary config for a single pool with reduced max_new_tokens and compaction, monitor 24h, then iterate.
Maya: agree. Quick config I plan to push to canary:
```
model: ridgeback18b
quant: int6
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  batch: {max_concurrent: 6, max_total_tokens: 2048}
runtime:
  slab_compact_interval_ms: 15000
  soft_slot_reserve: 0.15
  kv_prefix_evict: true
```
Jonah: small nit: set slab_compact_interval_ms to 12000 — we saw better tail behaviour there for similar layer shapes. Also add `slot_trim_on_eviction: true`.
Maya: updated. pushing config to canary pool-12 in 5m.
infra-bot: deploy initiated by maya to pool-12 (canary). build: ridgeback18b-int6-2026-03-21-09:12.
Priya: will watch OOM alerts and memory fragmentation dashboards. I'll add an alert for slab_free_ratio < 0.18 to fire early.
Alec: when we reduce max_new_tokens to 256, are we harming use-cases where customers expect long continuations? We need to document this as a canary-specific default.
Maya: yes will note in changelog and the rollout doc: "canary reduced max_new_tokens for stability; GA may differ".
Jonah: if the canary stabilizes, next step is try a kernel-affinity tweak: bind attention kernels to larger blocks to reduce temporary allocations at token boundaries (low-risk runtime flag).
Maya: also planning A/B eval on our 50-sample long-dialog benchmark to confirm quality unchanged. If quality delta <0.5% we'll proceed.
Priya: if OOMs persist after compaction + slot reserve, plan B is to enable per-session KV trimming for sessions >3k context length (evict older prefixes).
Maya: noted. I'll post an update after 6 hours of canary traffic.
infra-bot: canary metrics: 6h in, OOM count down 78% vs previous canary. slab_free_ratio median improved from 0.12 -> 0.21.
Maya: great signal. Quality A/B after 6h shows negligible delta (0.2% on our metric). Rolling config to additional canaries tomorrow morning.
Jonah: follow-up: schedule a short perf run to measure latency impact of slab compaction change (should be <3ms p95). I'll coordinate with eng-runtime.
Alec: thanks team — please add a short note to the release notes and notify support about canary defaults.
Maya: will do.
Jonah: one more: add a flag to allow customers to opt into the older max_new_tokens=512 behavior with explicit warning about OOM risk — useful for power users.
Maya: adding opt-in toggle to console docs.
Priya: closing loop: I'll keep alerting for 48h. If no regressions, we'll promote to staged rollout.
Maya: update: promoting tomorrow 08:00 PT if green. :rocket:
